newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil quiet, U.S. seen supporting LS cargos.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil quiet, U.S. seen supporting LS cargos.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were mostly inactive on Monday, with much of the continent enjoying a public holiday, but crude's strength kept notional prices firm, traders said.
The ARA barge market was almost completely dormant, with prompt high sulphur fuel oil heard unchanged at around $83/$85 fob a tonne.
But paper was firmer, with June at $86.50/$87.50, suggesting some upside when players return to their desks on Tuesday.
Low sulphur prices leapt $5 on Friday on a cargo deal at $95 fob, before crude's late rally, which entrenched higher prices.
Perceived U.S. demand for one percent cracked was the cause of the surge in cargo values, traders said. June swaps at $96/$97 broadly underlined that prices were steady on Monday.
"Demand is driven by the States. Its nothing to do with Enel at the moment," said one trader. "The market is on an upturn. Its a trend and whether the demand is really there or not doesn't matter."

Although U.S East Coast utility demand was seen falling this week and natural gas was becoming more attractively priced than one percent, Friday's buyers was heard trying to fix a vessel for trans-atlantic movement of his material.
